{{Quote|Did Kaan send you to kill me?''"<br />"''If you will not join the Brotherhood, I will leave your corpse on this barren and forgotten world.|Bane and Kas'im, just prior to their duel|<ref name="pod" />}}
In [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]], a '''lightsaber duel''' was fought on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Lehon/Legends|Lehon]] between two [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lords of the Sith]]: the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Sith Blademaster|Blademaster]] [[Kas'im]] and his former [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]], [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]]. Kas'im followed Bane to Lehon and found him in the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakatan]] [[Temple of the Ancients]], where he presented the [[Human/Legends|Human]] with the choice of either rejoining the [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]] to which Bane had once belonged, or making Lehon his final resting place. When Bane refused, an intense [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|lightsaber duel]] ensued.

Bane, who was considerably stronger in [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], maintained the offensive in the beginning of the duel. The tide turned when Kas'im split his [[Double-bladed lightsaber/Legends|double-bladed lightsaber]] into two [[Lightsaber/Legends|separate weapons]] and [[Jar'Kai/Legends|attacked]] his opponent with a previously unrealized degree of ferocity. Bane was forced onto the defensive, and was just barely able to maneuver his way out of the temple before Kas'im [[Telekinesis/Legends|blasted]] him with a wave of Force energy. Bane reciprocated the attack, and Kas'im absorbed its brunt by [[Force barrier/Legends|shielding himself]] with the Force. The temple entrance in which Kas'im stood, however, was obliterated by Bane's exertion, and the Twi'lek was unable to avoid being crushed to [[Death/Legends|death]] under the tons of rubble that fell upon him.

==Prelude==
{{Quote|The dark side cannot be united in the Brotherhood if he stands alone. I know he rejected you and the other Masters on Korriban. But you must make this offer once more.''"<br />"''And when he refuses?''"<br />"''Then you must kill him.|Dark Lords Kaan and Kas'im, regarding Darth Bane|<ref name="pod" />}}
In [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]], recently promoted [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]] abandoned the [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]] in the midst of a [[New Sith Wars|war]] with the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] and the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Convinced that the Brotherhood was nothing more than a flawed collection of individuals whose affirmation of [[The Force/Legends|the Force's]] [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] had diluted its potency, Bane left them to embark on his own search for [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] enlightenment. His quest led him to [[Lehon/Legends|Lehon]], or the "Unknown World," the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] where the [[Jedi Civil War]] of nearly [[3956 BBY|three thousand years]] prior had ended. Once there, he located an ancient [[Rakata/Legends|Rakatan]] [[Temple of the Ancients|temple]], wherein he discovered and began tedious exploration into the [[Darth Revan's Sith Holocron|Sith holocron]] of [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] [[Revan/Legends|Revan]].<ref name="pod" />

Meanwhile, the rest of the Brotherhood of Darkness had gathered on the planet [[Ruusan/Legends|Ruusan]] to engage in a [[Ruusan campaign|final campaign]] against the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi's]] [[Army of Light/Legends|Army of Light]]. [[Githany]], Bane's former [[Sith Master/Legends|mentor]], experienced a [[Force vision/Legends|Force premonition]] that involved Bane coming to Ruusan to destroy the entire Brotherhood. She informed the leader of the Sith, [[Skere Kaan|Kaan]], of this, and together they conspired to bring Bane back into the fold, lest the events of her vision become reality. Githany knew through her [[Force-bond/Legends|Force bond]] with Bane that he had gone to Lehon; to this end, Kaan enlisted the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Sith Blademaster|Blademaster]] [[Kas'im]] to find Bane and speak with his former [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]] on Kaan's behalf. Kaan's instructions were clear; if Bane could not be swayed, then Kas'im was to [[Death/Legends|kill]] him. The Twi'lek departed in a Sith [[Buzzard (starfighter)|Buzzard]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] and made his way to the Unknown World.<ref name="pod" />

==The duel==
===Part one===
{{Quote|Kaan is wrong. I will never follow him. I will never join the Brotherhood.''"<br />"[sigh] ''Then your life ends here.|Bane rejects Kas'im offer of returning to the Brotherhood|<ref name="pod" />}}
Kas'im homed in on the beacon from Darth Bane's stolen [[Starship/Legends|starship]], ''[[Valcyn/Legends|Valcyn]]'', and landed his starfighter nearby. He also [[Force sense/Legends|sensed]] Bane's presence, which he followed to the Temple of the Ancients, battling and killing a [[Rancor/Legends|rancor]] in the process. Kas'im found Darth Bane in the Temple's innermost chamber when he arrived, startling the man and causing him to activate his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]]. The two of them entered into a debate over the Brotherhood's ability to actually destroy the Jedi, and the Twi'lek ignited his [[Double-bladed lightsaber/Legends|double-bladed lightsaber]] as he attempted to convince Bane to partake in the war effort on Ruusan. Bane refused to be discouraged, and when he declined Kas'im's final offer to either rejoin the Brotherhood or die on Lehon, the Blademaster leaped in to engage Bane in [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|lightsaber combat]].<ref name="pod" />

[[File:Unkwldtemple.jpg|thumb|left|220px|The Temple of the Ancients, where Darth Bane and Kas'im dueled.]]
Darth Bane realized immediately from their initial exchange of blows that his former teacher had withheld his true ability from him during their training sessions. He was still able to just barely defend himself, which surprised Kas'im, who had advanced with the intention of bringing a quick end to the contest. The two men openly took notice of how the other's skills had improved since their last [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|duel]], and both reevaluated their tactics before resuming the battle. Kas'im engaged in a relentless offensive, but Bane surrendered completely to the dark side and with his lightsaber erected an impregnable defense. He then became the aggressor, driving Kas'im back and forcing him to retreat from the chamber. Bane leaped forward after him, and missed by less than a [[Centimeter/Legends|centimeter]] a blow that would have crippled his opponent. Kas'im switched several times between different strategies and dueling styles, but Bane anticipated each change and pressed his advantage. He had seen and developed counters for every technique the Twi'lek could implement with his saberstaff; that&mdash;combined with his superior knowledge of the Temple's interior layout&mdash;saw the duel rapidly progressing in Bane's favor.<ref name="pod" />

Kas'im, who had become desperate in the face of impending defeat, performed a series of acrobatic maneuvers as he attempted to escape Bane's assault. When he realized that his opponent was forcing him into a dead-end hallway, Kas'im used the Force to [[Telekinesis/Legends|blast]] open the door of an adjacent room, into which he dived. Noticing that the Twi'lek had effectively trapped himself, Bane stood in the doorway and relished in his apparent victory. Kas'im, exhausted though he was, admonished Darth Bane for not taking the opportunity to finish him. The Blademaster then twisted the hilt of his double-bladed weapon, which separated into two individual lightsabers, and [[Jar'Kai/Legends|attacked]] his adversary.<ref name="pod" />

===Duel's end===
{{Quote|I will follow you wherever you run. Wherever you go I will eventually find you and kill you. Don't live your life in fear, Bane. Better to end it now.''"<br />"''I agree.|Kas'im and Darth Bane|<ref name="pod" />}}
[[File:Bane.jpg|thumb|right|130px|Darth Bane]]
Bane was completely unfamiliar with Kas'im's two single-saber variant of [[Form IV/Legends|Ataru]] and was almost instantly outmatched. Despite his superior Force ability, what had once seemed like a certain victory for Bane turned into a fight for his life. Kas'im struck from all angles in his relentless onslaught, forcing Bane to concede more and more ground in a battle he believed he could no longer win. His only recourse was to work his way toward the Temple's only entrance in an effort to escape. Kas'im realized Bane's intent when the opening came into view, but he was momentarily unbalanced by a Force push from Bane as he back-flipped through the entrance onto the landing outside. Bane's flip had carried him too far, however, and he landed shakily on the edge of the landing's declining staircase. Kas'im followed with a telekinetic blast that knocked Bane down the stairs, but by [[Force barrier/Legends|shielding himself with the Force]], Bane was able to avoid sustaining serious injury.<ref name="pod" />

Kas'im stood under the Temple's archway and stared down at Darth Bane as he recovered. He told Bane that attempting to flee was futile, because Kas'im planned to pursue him wherever he went until which time the Twi'lek was able to kill him. He suggested that Bane end the duel then instead of prolonging the inevitable, and Bane, who had been gathering Force energy while Kas'im spoke, agreed as he unleashed it in a devastating Force wave against his foe. Kas'im shielded himself with the Force at the last moment, but he had not accounted for the destructive impact Bane's attack would have on the Temple's structure. The sheer power of the energies Bane released annihilated the Temple entrance, which collapsed and fell, crushing Kas'im below. Indifferent to the death of his former mentor, Bane left the Twi'lek under the rubble and set out for Ruusan.<ref name="pod" />

==Aftermath==
{{Quote|Kas'im is dead.''"<br />"''Dead? Was it the Jedi?''"<br />"''No. I sent him to parlay with Lord Bane. Kas'im thought he could convince him to join us. Instead, Bane killed him.|Lord Kaan and Githany|<ref name="pod" />}}
News of Kas'im's death preceded Darth Bane's own arrival on Ruusan and reached Lord Kaan via a [[message drone]] dispatched by Bane himself. Also included in the message were the details for creating the [[thought bomb]], an ancient Sith weapon that unleashed the pure destructive energy of the dark side. Disguised as a peace offering, Bane hoped that Kaan would detonate the thought bomb and in doing so obliterate every [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] being on Ruusan. When he finally arrived, Bane was able to convince Kaan to use the thought bomb, which he employed during the [[Seventh Battle of Ruusan|final battle]] for dominion over Ruusan. As Bane had anticipated, the thought bomb wiped out Kaan and the entire Brotherhood of Darkness, as well as most of the planet-side Jedi; Bane had indeed destroyed the Brotherhood just as Githany had foreseen. The elimination of his rivals paved the way for Darth Bane to create a new [[Order of the Sith Lords|Sith Order]] of his own design&mdash;one that, instead of dispersing the strength of the dark side throughout numerous Dark Lords, focused the power of the Force in [[Rule of Two/Legends|two individuals]]: one Sith Master to embody that power, and a single Sith apprentice to crave it.<ref name="pod" />

==Behind the scenes==
The duel on Lehon appeared in the first novel of author [[Drew Karpyshyn]]'s [[Star Wars: Darth Bane Trilogy|''Darth Bane Trilogy'']], titled [[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction|''Path of Destruction'']]. The event was later alluded to in ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', wherein Kas'im's entry notes his death at the hands of Darth Bane.
